# Quiver Mutation Database (QMD)

> A curated, citable database of quivers, their exchange matrices, and mutation
> classes, with rigorously defined invariants and transparent computational
> provenance. Read-only public API, no authentication, CC-BY-4.0.

Site: https://quivermutationdb.org · API base: https://quivermutationdb.org/api
OpenAPI: https://quivermutationdb.org/api/openapi.json
MCP server (Streamable HTTP, no auth): https://quivermutationdb.org/mcp
Definitions of every property: https://quivermutationdb.org/wiki
Maintainer: Blake Jackson <jackson@icarm.io>

## Identifiers

- Quiver: `Q.n{rank}.{sha256[:16]}` — hash of the lex-min canonical exchange
  matrix (row-major lexicographically smallest relabeling). Two matrices are
  the same quiver iff they have the same id. `GET /api/lookup?matrix=[[...]]`
  computes it for any labeling and returns the row if present.
- The census contains connected quivers only.
- Mutation class: `MC.n{rank}.{sha256[:16]}` — hash of the lex-min matrix over
  the whole explored orbit. Ids are frozen; a re-keying would be announced.
- Exchange matrix: row-major skew-symmetric integer matrix; `b_ij > 0` means
  `b_ij` arrows from vertex i to vertex j.

## Reading the data

- `GET /api/stats` — totals and, per rank, how the data was generated:
  weight bound, node cap, `generator` (`orderly` = exact census of the cell,
  `sample` = uniform sample of labeled matrices, not uniform over isomorphism
  classes), `census_size` (exact number of quivers in the cell), pipeline
  version, date. Compare `distinct_quivers` with `census_size` for coverage.
- `GET /api/quivers?rank=4&is_acyclic=true&limit=100` — filter/sort/page.
  Every list returns `next_cursor`; pass it back as `?cursor=` (opaque).
  `scope=labelings` gives one row per labeled exchange matrix.
  Page with `next_cursor`, not by computing pages from `total`: counting a
  filtered cut of a 42.5 M-row rank is a full table scan, so the count stops
  at 10,000 and the response sets `total_is_lower_bound: true`. Add
  `?total=exact` when you genuinely need the true figure — it is slow by
  design. A rank-only cut is answered from stored aggregates and is exact.
- `GET /api/quivers/{id}` · `GET /api/quivers/{id}/labelings`
- `GET /api/classes` · `GET /api/classes/{id}` — invariants + provenance +
  first page of members; `GET /api/classes/{id}/quivers` (distinct members,
  canonical first) · `GET /api/classes/{id}/labelings` (every labeled matrix).
- `GET /api/classes/by-slug/markov` · `GET /api/nicknames` — curated names.
  `GET /api/quivers?has_name=true` is every quiver in a NAMED class (61
  classes): the automatic Dynkin/surface `label` plus the curated nicknames.
  `has_nickname=true` is the narrower curated set only (21). E6, E7, E8 and
  every A_n/D_n are named automatically and have no nickname, so prefer
  `has_name` unless you specifically want the hand-curated entries.
- `GET /api/random/quiver` · `GET /api/random/class`
- Bulk pull, FILTERED cut: `GET /api/export.ndjson?rank=4&limit=5000` then
  follow the `X-Next-Cursor` header until it is empty. Omit `limit` to stream
  the whole cut. `GET /api/export?...` is the same cut as CSV.
- Bulk pull, WHOLE DATABASE: use `GET /api/bulk` instead. The full census is
  pre-rendered as one gzipped NDJSON file per rank in object storage — no
  database work, free egress, resumable (`curl -C - -O`), with sha256
  checksums in the manifest. The rows are byte-for-byte identical to
  `/api/export.ndjson`. Do not page 50 M rows through the API when you want
  all of them; download the files.

## What changed, and when

Data and API changes are recorded in the repository's `CHANGELOG.md`
(<https://github.com/quivermutationdb/api/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md>). Two
guarantees you can rely on: `Q.*` / `MC.*` identifiers are frozen and never
re-key for the same object, and response shapes are additive — fields may be
added, but existing fields do not change meaning or vanish without an entry.
If you cache results, cache them by id.

## Semantics you must respect

- Three-state properties (`is_mutation_acyclic`, `is_banff`, `is_louise`,
  `is_p_prime`, `is_finite_confirmed`, ...): `true`, `false`, or `null` =
  unknown (the search was truncated). `null` is never a "no".
- `mutation_finite` on every quiver: `true` / `false` / `null` (unknown). It is
  known even for quivers whose class was not explored (`explored: false`,
  `mc_id: null`): a rank ≥ 3 quiver with an entry |b_ij| ≥ 3 is mutation-
  infinite (Derksen–Owen).
- `exploration` on explored classes: `complete` (finite), `bound` (a
  mutation crossed |b_ij| ≤ 2, which proves mutation-infinite at rank ≥ 3),
  `truncated` (node cap reached; finiteness unknown). Class members are
  distinct quivers; `class_size` (labeled orbit) and `labelings` exist only
  for small finite classes (`labelings_stored`).
- `is_mutation_finite=true` returns only proved-finite classes;
  `=false` only proved-infinite ones. Undetermined classes match neither.
- Please cite: Blake Jackson, *Quiver Mutation Database*,
  https://quivermutationdb.org (CC-BY-4.0). Citation text: /about.
